project: Namias Portfolio - Smart Blog Content Pipeline
summary: Local-first blog content pipeline where every blog post (published and unpublished) lives as a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter in content/blog/. Authors write and review locally, then sync to Sanity CMS for publishing. Includes specialized agent skills for creating, editing, reviewing, diffing, and publishing posts. The Sanity Studio remains the source of truth for live content, but the local MD files become the authoring and review layer on top.
narrative: Today all blog content lives exclusively in Sanity CMS. There is no local representation of posts, no way to review drafts before they go live, no version history outside Sanity's built-in revisions, and no way for coding agents to author or edit posts programmatically. The existing add-a-blog-post skill only describes the manual Sanity Studio UI workflow. This PRD introduces a local-first content layer: every blog post (published or draft) is stored as a Markdown file in content/blog/ with YAML frontmatter containing all metadata (title, slug, excerpt, tags, date, published status, SEO fields, author, categories). A bidirectional sync script keeps local files and Sanity documents in sync. New agent skills let you create, edit, preview, diff, and publish posts entirely from the CLI. The workflow becomes: write locally as MD → review the diff → sync to Sanity → publish. This gives the owner full control over what goes live, enables git-based version history for all content, and lets coding agents participate in the content lifecycle.
principles: Local-first: content/blog/ is the authoring surface; Sanity is the publishing surface
Bidirectional sync: pull from Sanity to local, push from local to Sanity, with conflict detection
Review before publish: no post goes live without an explicit publish command after review
Git-versioned: every content change is a git commit with meaningful history
Frontmatter-driven: all metadata lives in YAML frontmatter; the MD body is the post content
Backward-compatible: existing Sanity posts are importable; existing GROQ queries are unchanged
Skill-augmented: specialized agent skills handle create, edit, review, sync, and publish
Safe: unpublished drafts are clearly marked, never synced to Sanity unless explicitly requested
Type-safe: frontmatter schema is validated at build time; tsc, lint, vitest stay green
No comments in code: documentation lives in the PRD and skills only

designDecisions.choice: content/blog/ at the repo root, with one .md file per post. File naming: {slug}.md (e.g., content/blog/hello-world.md).
designDecisions.rationale: Flat directory is simple. Slug-based filenames make lookup trivial. No nesting needed for a personal blog with <100 posts.

designDecisions.choice: YAML frontmatter with fields matching the Sanity post schema: title, slug, excerpt, metaTitle, metaDescription, featured, readTime, publishedAt, publishAt, published, author, categories, tags, coverImage, sourceId. Body is the Markdown content below the frontmatter.
designDecisions.rationale: 1:1 mapping with Sanity schema means sync is straightforward. No translation layer needed.

designDecisions.choice: Bidirectional with explicit direction flags: --push (local → Sanity), --pull (Sanity → local), --diff (compare). Default is dry-run (show what would change).
designDecisions.rationale: Explicit direction prevents accidents. Dry-run default means you always see what will happen before it happens.

designDecisions.choice: Last-write-wins with --force flag. Without --force, conflicts are reported and skipped. The sync script compares updatedAt timestamps and content hashes.
designDecisions.rationale: Simple and predictable. --force gives the owner explicit override when needed.

designDecisions.choice: Posts with published: false in frontmatter are local-only by default. They are only pushed to Sanity when --include-drafts flag is set. They never appear on the live site.
designDecisions.rationale: Drafts stay invisible until explicitly pushed. This prevents accidental publishing.

designDecisions.choice: Five specialized skills: (1) blog-create — generate a new MD file with frontmatter template, (2) blog-edit — modify existing post content, (3) blog-review — show diff between local and Sanity, (4) blog-sync — push/pull between local and Sanity, (5) blog-publish — mark as published and sync. Each skill is a standalone .agents/skills/ entry.
designDecisions.rationale: Separation of concerns. Each skill does one thing well. Agents can load the right skill for the task.

designDecisions.choice: The sync script uses the existing Sanity client from src/lib/sanity/client.ts (or a new scripts/lib/sanity-client.ts if isolation is needed). No new Sanity tokens.
designDecisions.rationale: Reuse existing credentials and client config. No new secrets to manage.

designDecisions.choice: One-time import script: scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs. Pulls all post documents from Sanity, converts Portable Text to Markdown, writes to content/blog/. Skips if file already exists (no overwrite without --force).
designDecisions.rationale: Bootstraps the local content directory from existing Sanity data. Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.

designDecisions.choice: New Frontmatter type in src/types/blog.ts that mirrors BlogPost but uses local field names. The sync script translates between Frontmatter and Sanity document shapes.
designDecisions.rationale: Type safety for frontmatter validation. Clear translation boundary between local and CMS representations.

designDecisions.choice: UTF-8 with LF line endings. Frontmatter delimiters: --- (standard YAML). Markdown body uses GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) with tables, task lists, and fenced code blocks.
designDecisions.rationale: Standard conventions. GFM is universally supported and matches the existing blog renderer (remark-gfm).

epics.title: Plan, types & schema
epics.summary: Write the PRD, define the Frontmatter TypeScript type, validate the content directory structure, and create the frontmatter schema.

stories.title: Write PRD for smart blog content pipeline
stories.details: Author prd.blog-smart-content.json in docs/prd/. Include all epics, stories, success metrics, non-goals, and design decisions.

stories.title: Create Frontmatter TypeScript type
stories.details: Create src/types/blog.ts with a Frontmatter interface that mirrors the BlogPost type but is optimized for local MD files. Fields: title (string), slug (string), excerpt (string), metaTitle (string?), metaDescription (string?), featured (boolean), readTime (string?), publishedAt (string), publishAt (string?), published (boolean), author (string), categories (string[]), tags (string[]), coverImage (string?), sourceId (string?). Export the type.

stories.title: Create frontmatter validation schema
stories.details: Create scripts/lib/frontmatter-schema.ts with a zod schema that validates frontmatter. Required fields: title, slug, excerpt, publishedAt, published, author, tags. Validate at sync time and in tests.

stories.title: Create content/blog/ directory
stories.details: Create content/blog/ with a .gitkeep file and a README.md explaining the structure. Add content/blog/ to .gitignore if needed (no — it should be tracked in git).

epics.title: Sync scripts
epics.summary: Build the bidirectional sync scripts: push (local → Sanity), pull (Sanity → local), diff (compare), and the one-time import script.

stories.title: Create Sanity client for scripts
stories.details: Create scripts/lib/sanity-client.ts that initializes a Sanity client using the existing env vars (SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN, SANITY_PROJECT_ID, SANITY_DATASET). Export the client for use by sync scripts.

stories.title: Create MD file parser
stories.details: Create scripts/lib/md-parser.ts. Functions: parseMdFile(filePath) → { frontmatter: Frontmatter, body: string }, writeMdFile(filePath, frontmatter, body), listMdFiles(dir) → filePath[]. Use gray-matter for YAML parsing.

stories.title: Create Portable Text to Markdown converter
stories.details: Create scripts/lib/portable-text-to-md.ts. Convert Sanity Portable Text blocks to GFM Markdown. Handle: headings (h1-h4), blockquotes, bullet/number lists, bold/italic/code marks, links, inline images, code blocks. Reuse or adapt the existing portableTextToMarkdown from src/lib/cms-content.server.ts if possible.

stories.title: Create Markdown to Portable Text converter
stories.details: Create scripts/lib/md-to-portable-text.ts. Convert GFM Markdown back to Sanity Portable Text blocks. Handle: headings, blockquotes, lists, marks, links, images, code blocks. This is the inverse of S-1.3.

stories.title: Create pull script (Sanity → local)
stories.details: Create scripts/blog-sync.mjs with --pull flag. Fetch all post documents from Sanity via GROQ query. For each post: convert Portable Text body to Markdown, map fields to frontmatter, write to content/blog/{slug}.md. Skip if file exists (unless --force). Report what was created/updated/skipped.

stories.title: Create push script (local → Sanity)
stories.details: Create scripts/blog-sync.mjs with --push flag. Read all .md files from content/blog/. For each: parse frontmatter, convert Markdown body to Portable Text, create or update Sanity document via Sanity client. Only push posts where published: true (unless --include-drafts). Dry-run by default (show what would change). Report what would be created/updated/deleted.

stories.title: Create diff script
stories.details: Create scripts/blog-sync.mjs with --diff flag. Compare local MD files against Sanity documents. Show: new local posts (not in Sanity), updated local posts (content differs), deleted local posts (in Sanity but not local). Use content hashing for comparison.

stories.title: Create one-time import script
stories.details: Create scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs. Fetch all post documents from Sanity. For each: convert Portable Text to Markdown, write to content/blog/{slug}.md with frontmatter. Skip if file exists. Support --force to overwrite. This is a one-time bootstrap tool.

stories.title: Add npm scripts for blog sync
stories.details: Add to package.json: 'blog:sync' (node scripts/blog-sync.mjs), 'blog:pull' (node scripts/blog-sync.mjs --pull), 'blog:push' (node scripts/blog-sync.mjs --push), 'blog:diff' (node scripts/blog-sync.mjs --diff), 'blog:import' (node scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs).

epics.title: Agent skills
epics.summary: Create five specialized agent skills for the blog content lifecycle: create, edit, review, sync, and publish.

stories.title: Create blog-create skill
stories.details: Create .agents/skills/blog-create/SKILL.md. Skill generates a new blog post MD file in content/blog/ with a frontmatter template. Steps: (1) ask for title, (2) generate slug from title, (3) set defaults (published: false, date: now, author: 'PP Namias'), (4) create the MD file with frontmatter + placeholder body, (5) confirm the file was created.

stories.title: Create blog-edit skill
stories.details: Create .agents/skills/blog-edit/SKILL.md. Skill modifies an existing blog post. Steps: (1) find the MD file by slug or title, (2) read current content, (3) apply the requested edits to body or frontmatter, (4) write the updated file, (5) confirm changes. Support editing body, tags, excerpt, published status, and other frontmatter fields.

stories.title: Create blog-review skill
stories.details: Create .agents/skills/blog-review/SKILL.md. Skill shows the current state of all blog posts and their sync status. Steps: (1) list all MD files in content/blog/, (2) for each, show title, published status, date, (3) run diff against Sanity to show which are synced/unsynced/modified, (4) highlight any validation errors in frontmatter.

stories.title: Create blog-sync skill
stories.details: Create .agents/skills/blog-sync/SKILL.md. Skill runs the sync script with the appropriate flags. Steps: (1) run --diff first to show current state, (2) ask user to confirm push or pull, (3) execute the sync, (4) report results. Default to dry-run. Support --include-drafts flag.

stories.title: Create blog-publish skill
stories.details: Create .agents/skills/blog-publish/SKILL.md. Skill publishes a post by setting published: true in frontmatter and syncing to Sanity. Steps: (1) find the post by slug, (2) show the post content for final review, (3) set published: true and publishedAt: now in frontmatter, (4) run sync --push for that post, (5) verify it appears on the live site.

epics.title: Tests
epics.summary: Add tests for the frontmatter schema, MD parser, sync logic, and Portable Text converters.

stories.title: Add frontmatter schema tests
stories.details: Create src/__tests__/scripts/frontmatter-schema.test.ts. Test: valid frontmatter passes, missing required fields fail, invalid dates fail, published is boolean, tags is array of strings.

stories.title: Add MD parser tests
stories.details: Create src/__tests__/scripts/md-parser.test.ts. Test: parseMdFile extracts frontmatter and body correctly, writeMdFile creates valid MD, listMdFiles returns all .md files, handles missing file gracefully.

stories.title: Add Portable Text to MD converter tests
stories.details: Create src/__tests__/scripts/portable-text-to-md.test.ts. Test: headings, blockquotes, lists, marks (bold/italic/code), links, inline images, code blocks. Compare against expected GFM output.

stories.title: Add MD to Portable Text converter tests
stories.details: Create src/__tests__/scripts/md-to-portable-text.test.ts. Test: headings, blockquotes, lists, marks, links, images, code blocks. Round-trip test: MD → Portable Text → MD should preserve content.

stories.title: Add sync script integration tests
stories.details: Create src/__tests__/scripts/blog-sync.test.ts. Test: --pull creates MD files from mocked Sanity data, --push creates Sanity documents from MD files, --diff shows correct status, --force overwrites existing, dry-run does not modify files. Mock the Sanity client.

epics.title: Import existing content
epics.summary: Run the one-time import to bootstrap content/blog/ from existing Sanity posts, then verify the imported files.

stories.title: Run import script against Sanity
stories.details: Execute node scripts/import-sanity-posts.mjs. Verify it pulls all existing published posts from Sanity and writes them as MD files in content/blog/. Check that frontmatter matches the Sanity document fields.

stories.title: Verify imported MD files
stories.details: Review the imported MD files: check frontmatter validity, confirm body content is correct Markdown, verify slug-based filenames, ensure no data loss from the Portable Text → Markdown conversion.

stories.title: Commit imported content
stories.details: git add content/blog/ and commit with message: 'content(blog): import existing Sanity posts as local MD files'. This establishes the initial content baseline.

epics.title: Documentation & integration
epics.summary: Update AGENTS.md with new skills, add blog content workflow documentation, and update the existing add-a-blog-post skill.

stories.title: Update AGENTS.md with new skills
stories.details: Add blog-create, blog-edit, blog-review, blog-sync, blog-publish to the Skills table in AGENTS.md. Add a new 'Content Workflow' section describing the local-first blog pipeline.

stories.title: Update add-a-blog-post skill
stories.details: Update .agents/skills/add-a-blog-post/SKILL.md to reference the new blog-create skill as the recommended approach. Keep the Sanity Studio steps as a fallback.

stories.title: Add content/blog/ README
stories.details: Create content/blog/README.md explaining the directory structure, frontmatter schema, and how to create/edit/publish posts. Include examples of valid frontmatter.

epics.title: Verification
epics.summary: Run the full quality gate: typecheck, lint, vitest, react-doctor, and manual verification of the content pipeline.

stories.title: Run tsc, eslint, vitest
stories.details: Run: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, npm run test -- --run. All must pass with the new tests included.

stories.title: Run react-doctor
stories.details: Run npm run doctor. Score must stay at 100/100. If a finding lands, fix it in the same PR following the fix-react-doctor-finding skill.

stories.title: End-to-end content pipeline test
stories.details: Manual verification: (1) create a new post via blog-create skill, (2) edit it via blog-edit skill, (3) review via blog-review skill, (4) sync via blog-sync skill, (5) verify the post appears in Sanity Studio, (6) verify /blog route renders the new post.

openQuestions: Should the sync script support incremental sync (only changed posts) or always do a full sync? The PRD plans full sync with content hashing for comparison.
Should the Portable Text converters be in a shared utility or duplicated in scripts/? The PRD plans separate files in scripts/lib/ to avoid coupling with the main app bundle.
Should the blog-create skill ask for all frontmatter fields interactively, or use smart defaults? The PRD plans smart defaults with an option to customize.
Should content/blog/ be in .gitignore or tracked in git? The PRD plans tracked in git — this is the whole point of local-first content.
Should the diff command show full content diffs or just status (new/modified/deleted)? The PRD plans status by default with --full for content diffs.
